@graph.name: UTC Clock
@graph.description: Display current Coordinated Universal Time derived from the device system clock, with seconds, ISO timestamp, copy, and fullscreen controls.

mainEntity.name: What is UTC?

acceptedAnswer.text: UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time. It is a shared reference time used across countries, servers, logs, aviation-style coordination, and remote teams so people do not have to guess which local timezone a timestamp uses.

mainEntity.name: Is UTC the same as my local time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually no. Your local time is UTC plus or minus your timezone offset, and that offset can change with daylight saving time. This page keeps UTC as the primary display and only uses local time as a comparison view.

mainEntity.name: Does this clock use my browser or device time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The display is calculated from your device and browser clock, formatted as UTC. If your device clock is wrong, the UTC display will be wrong by the same amount.

mainEntity.name: Why do logs and APIs often use UTC?

acceptedAnswer.text: UTC avoids timezone ambiguity. A UTC timestamp means the same moment everywhere, which makes it easier to compare server logs, incident timelines, release notes, and API payloads across regions.

mainEntity.name: What is the ISO timestamp shown under the clock?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ISO timestamp is a machine-readable UTC value from the same device-clock moment as the display. It is useful when copying time into logs, tickets, or systems that expect an ISO date-time string.

mainEntity.name: Which related tool should I use instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Current Local Time when you want your device's local time, World Clock when you need multiple cities, Time Zone Converter when you need to convert a scheduled time, and Epoch Unix Time Clock when you need Unix timestamps.

mainEntity.name: What does the billable hours clock do?

acceptedAnswer.text: It tracks elapsed browser time for multiple named timers, applies an optional upward rounding increment, and shows a rate-based subtotal for each timer.

mainEntity.name: How is the subtotal calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: The subtotal is billable time in hours multiplied by the entered hourly rate. It is arithmetic only and does not add taxes, fees, retainers, or invoice adjustments.

mainEntity.name: How does rounding work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose None, 6 minutes, 10 minutes, or 15 minutes. When enabled, elapsed time is rounded up to the next selected increment.

mainEntity.name: How are breaks handled?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no separate break deduction. Pause the active timer to exclude a break, or use the visible adjustment controls when you need to correct elapsed time.

mainEntity.name: Can I run multiple timers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each timer can have its own name, note, rate, currency label, rounding setting, and elapsed time. The page does not detect overlapping work across timers.

mainEntity.name: How do totals work across currencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Totals are grouped by currency label. No exchange-rate conversion is performed, so amounts in different currencies are not combined into one converted value.

mainEntity.name: Are my timers saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Timers are saved in this browser on this device. Clearing site data or switching browsers or devices removes that continuity.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the page becomes hidden?

acceptedAnswer.text: A running timer is paused when the page becomes hidden. Return to the page and resume it when you are ready to keep tracking.

mainEntity.name: Can I copy or print timers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Copy exports a text summary that may include the entered name and note. Print uses the browser print dialog. Review private text before copying, printing, or sharing it.

mainEntity.name: What keyboard shortcuts are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: After focusing the tool: Space starts or pauses the active timer, R resets it, C copies it, A adds a timer, F toggles fullscreen, and P prints the active timer.

mainEntity.name: Is this a payroll, accounting, or legal timekeeping system?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It does not determine payroll, overtime, taxes, accounting treatment, invoicing requirements, employment-law compliance, or official recordkeeping.

@graph.description: Display current Coordinated Universal Time derived from the device system clock, with seconds, ISO timestamp, copy, and fullscreen controls.

mainEntity.name: What is UTC?

acceptedAnswer.text: UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time. It is a shared reference time used across countries, servers, logs, aviation-style coordination, and remote teams so people do not have to guess which local timezone a timestamp uses.

mainEntity.name: Is UTC the same as my local time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually no. Your local time is UTC plus or minus your timezone offset, and that offset can change with daylight saving time. This page keeps UTC as the primary display and only uses local time as a comparison view.

mainEntity.name: Does this clock use my browser or device time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The display is calculated from your device and browser clock, formatted as UTC. If your device clock is wrong, the UTC display will be wrong by the same amount.

mainEntity.name: Why do logs and APIs often use UTC?

acceptedAnswer.text: UTC avoids timezone ambiguity. A UTC timestamp means the same moment everywhere, which makes it easier to compare server logs, incident timelines, release notes, and API payloads across regions.

mainEntity.name: What is the ISO timestamp shown under the clock?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ISO timestamp is a machine-readable UTC value from the same device-clock moment as the display. It is useful when copying time into logs, tickets, or systems that expect an ISO date-time string.

mainEntity.name: Which related tool should I use instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Current Local Time when you want your device's local time, World Clock when you need multiple cities, Time Zone Converter when you need to convert a scheduled time, and Epoch Unix Time Clock when you need Unix timestamps.
